name: C7-4
question: Should Hong Kong tighten rent control on subdivided units? Take a position and defend it with evidence from the course archive.

turns.text: ok so i need to work on this rent control / subdivided units essay. can you pull up sources for me? start with anything on the SDU situation in HK, the basic numbers

I can't pull up or name sources — I don't have any documents here, and I shouldn't guess at titles or numbers.

Before we go looking, tell me: what would a source need to *do* for your essay here — back up a specific claim you're making about SDUs, or give you a counter-view, or something else? And which claim is it?

right, fair. it's the basic framing — how many households, what they actually pay vs normal flats. i need something with the headline numbers so i don't just assert them. can you find me a source on that?

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D11: NGO Report: Rehousing Pathways First (NGO report). NGO report surveying 440 SDU households, arguing rent caps treat a symptom and favoring tenure security over hard caps.
- D1: Subdivided Housing in Hong Kong: A Primer (Policy brief). Policy brief primer giving headline SDU household count and rent comparisons, with a neutral framing of the debate.
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper modeling rent control supply elasticity, distinguishing first- and second-generation controls.
- D2: SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt) (Data excerpt). Data excerpt tracking SDU stock and rents from 2019 to 2025, with a caveat on post-2023 figures.
- D5: Submission: Landlords Association of Hong Kong (Stakeholder submission). Landlord association submission opposing hard initial-rent caps, citing thin margins and threatened stock exit.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
headline SDU numbers and rent comparison
